title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's sequel to La Longue Marche (1981), 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. He studies the 'loop relation' that a candidate Galois-type automorphism of the profinite Teichmüller tower must satisfy at low levels, and here pushes it down to a linear quotient where the target group is Sl(2,Ẑ) inside Gl(2,Ẑ). The notation is as follows. ρ is the order-3 automorphism coming from the cyclic permutation of 0, 1, ∞; it is conjugation by an order-6 element whose cube is −1, so ρ^3 = −1 as a matrix while ρ has order 3 as an automorphism. σ_∞ is the involution; the next page shows f σ_∞(f)^{-1} = f·ᵗf, so σ_∞(f) = ᵗf^{-1}. l_0 is the loop around 0, and ρ(l_0) = l_1 holds exactly in Sl(2,Ẑ). ν ∈ Ẑ is an exponent.

Data: α_0 ∈ Gl(2,Ẑ) with det α_0 = ±1, and f ∈ Sl(2,Ẑ), with signs chosen arbitrarily. Set ξ = α_0 ρ(α_0)^{-1} and φ = f σ_∞(f)^{-1}; both lie in Sl(2,Ẑ). The previous page showed that ξ = ε l_0^ν φ holds for a well-defined sign ε ∈ {±1}, which is relation (44). The open question is whether ε = +1.

The page introduces g = σ_∞(f)^{-1} l_1^ν ρ(f) = (l_0^ν f)^{-1} (l_0^ν φ) ρ(l_0^ν f). This is the ρ-twisted conjugate of l_0^ν φ by l_0^ν f.
- If ξ = ε l_0^ν φ, then l_0^ν φ = ε α_0 ρ(α_0)^{-1}, hence g = ε α ρ(α)^{-1} with α = (l_0^ν f)^{-1} α_0 = f^{-1} l_0^{-ν} α_0.
- So g is (up to sign) a ρ-coboundary.
- Hence g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = ε^3 α ρ^3(α)^{-1} = ε, because ρ^3 = id as an automorphism (it is conjugation by a central element).
- Therefore 'ξ = l_0^ν φ in Sl(2,Ẑ)' is equivalent to the 'triangle/cocycle' identity g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1. Grothendieck explicitly leaves this in suspense and records the formulas as (45), the 'case h = 1'.

The margin note proposes renormalizing g by the sign so that g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1 holds outright, with the remark ε = ε_0.

He then begins the symmetric system (46), the 'case g = 1':
- β_0, f ∈ Sl(2,Ẑ);
- η = β_0 σ_∞(β_0)^{-1}, a σ_∞-coboundary;
- ψ = (probably f) ρ(f)^{-1};
- h = f^{-1} l_0^ν σ_∞(ρ(f)) = …, left unfinished.

The following page (364) specializes the case h = 1 to explicit 2×2 matrices with entries in Ẑ. There φ = f ᵗf is symmetric, and ξ = ε l_0^ν φ becomes the 'relation des lacets'. The structure throughout is the familiar one: the hexagon-type relation is a nonabelian Z/3-cocycle condition for ρ, and the 2-cycle relation is a σ_∞-cocycle condition (cf. the GT relations f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1 and the triangle relation).
errors: The transcription's g = σ_∞(f)^{-1} l_0^ν ρ(f) does not equal the second expression (l_0^ν f)^{-1}(l_0^ν φ)ρ(l_0^ν f). That expression yields σ_∞(f)^{-1} l_1^ν ρ(f), using ρ(l_0) = l_1. The manuscript most likely reads l_1^ν; otherwise the first form is a slip.

The stated equivalence is only valid using the prior result that ξ = ε l_0^ν φ holds for some sign. In general, g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = ±1 does not imply that g is a ρ-coboundary: nonabelian H^1(Z/3, Sl(2,Ẑ)) need not be trivial. Grothendieck implicitly relies on the previous page, so there is no real gap.
In (46), 'ψ = φ ρ(f)^{-1}' is likely a misreading of ψ = f ρ(f)^{-1}, which is the symmetric analogue of φ = f σ_∞(f)^{-1}.

ideas.what: Reformulating the loop relation ξ = l_0^ν φ as the ρ-cocycle (triangle) condition g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1 via a twisted change of variables g = ε α ρ(α)^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: nonabelian 1-cocycles/coboundaries for Z/3 and Z/2 actions; hexagon and 2-cycle relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990–91); Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura for low-level/linear images
ideas.where_published: Spirit appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) and La Longue Marche (1981); this explicit computation is unpublished

ideas.what: Sign bookkeeping when lifting from PSL2 to Sl(2,Ẑ): ρ has order 3 as an automorphism but its implementing matrix cubes to −1, so relations hold only up to a sign ε
ideas.modern_name: central extension SL2 → PSL2; sign ambiguity in lifting braid/mapping class relations

ideas.what: Splitting the problem into two symmetric cases: h = 1 (ρ-twisted) and g = 1 (σ_∞-twisted)

missed.claim: Whether the sign ε equals +1, i.e. whether the loop relation holds exactly in Sl(2,Ẑ) rather than up to −1, is explicitly left open. The page reduces it to g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1.
missed.quote: la question de la validité de la formule ξ = l_0^ν φ dans Sl(2,Ẑ) équivaut à celle de la validité de la formule gρ(g)ρ²(g) = 1, que nous laissons en suspens pour le moment
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor. It concerns how GT-type relations lift through the central extension SL2(Ẑ) → PSL2(Ẑ), relevant to genus-one/elliptic versions of GT (Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto, Enriquez). It is probably resolvable by a short computation and likely known implicitly.

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine cocycle and sign manipulation in Grothendieck's pre-Drinfeld work on the loop relations. Its main interest is as documentation that he worked with the hexagon/2-cycle structure as twisted cocycle conditions. That fact is already acknowledged historically (Grothendieck anticipating GT). Nothing here appears to be a new result.
transcription_corrections: In the definition of g, read σ_∞(f)^{-1} l_1^ν ρ(f) (l_1, not l_0), consistent with ρ(l_0) = l_1.
Read ξ = α_0 ρ(α_0)^{-1} in the displayed system (the transcription is correct here); on the previous page 'ξ = α_0 ρ(α_0)' lacks the inverse.
In (46), ψ is probably f ρ(f)^{-1}, not φ ρ(f)^{-1}.
'singulières signes' should be 'signes arbitraires' (same phrasing as in the first system: 'signes arbitraires, à leur choix').
In l_0^ν the exponent is ν (Greek nu), written like a superscript v/∨ in the previous page's transcription.
